note: A single shaded back-in site on a short dirt driveway off PA 144, about half a mile south of Osborne Road and 3.1 miles north of Cross Fork Creek Road. The agency warns that access is through guard rails and that RVs may not have good ingress. The booking page sells it for RVs and trailers, while the DCNR campsite map layer marks it as having no trailer access. Stone fire ring; no table, toilet or water. Pack out trash. --Claude
summary: Site page re-read: 030 Rte 144 Pines still listed, Drive-In, RV/Tent/Trailer categories, max vehicle and equipment length 40 ft, back-in dirt driveway 40 ft, grades Slight; count 1 and 40 ft confirmed, pull_through false and a sites note added. Year-round confirmed; sells in all five windows. Fees confirmed, $6.50 reservation fee added; hookups and facilities none. Imagery (Esri and PASDA leaf-off): pin about 75 m south-east of PA 144 under closed mixed canopy; neither the driveway nor the pad is resolved, pin not moved. NHD: nearest stream 86 m; not waterfront.
flags: CRITERIA flag (single-site entry; kept with the wording in the note, the owner decides): the page says 'Caution: This campsite is accessed by state forest dirt or gravel roads and may not be suitable for some low-clearance vehicles or large RVs. Access is through guard rails, RVs may not have good ingress.' The guard-rail sentence is site-specific agency wording about RV access. It sits beside 'Max Vehicle Length: 40' and the RV category. No Severe grade, 4WD line or closure, so ruling 11's automatic grounds do not apply; if it is read as ruling RVs out, the entry has no site left.

Ruling 5 applied: the booking page lists 'RV Site, Tent Site, Trailer Site' with Max Vehicle Length 40, while the DCNR GIS record for 030 Rte 144 Pines says 'TrailerAccess: No'. Kept, both statements in the note.

Pin: the page calls the driveway 'short' and lists 'Driveway Length: 40', but the page's coordinates, its GIS Details and the DCNR GIS point all put the site about 75 m from the edge of PA 144. Under canopy on both image sets, so no better point can be given; not moved.

Agency access statements (ruling 11: nothing measured, no road surface, gate or bridge research): 'Site Grade: Slight', 'Driveway Grade: Slight', 'Driveway Surface: Dirt', 'Site Height/Overhead Clearance: 20'. No Severe grade, no 4WD or wet-weather statement, no closure. The page also carries the district-wide 'Road and Travel Alert' and '4WD vehicles may be recommended for some sites year-round, check notes' boilerplate (this site's notes say nothing about 4WD).
Waterfront: NHD's nearest flowline is an unnamed stream 86 m from the pin; Kettle Creek is about 155 m away. Forest between. Stays not waterfront.

ATV check (ruling 1): the site page(s) say nothing about ATVs and do not call the ground a parking area. The DCNR Susquehannock ATV Trail brochure names five trailheads (District Office, Sunken Branch, Route 44, Rock Run, Lyman); none is this site. The camp at the Rock Run trailhead is a separate site, '029 Rock Run ATV' in the DCNR GIS layer, not part of this entry. Kept.
NAME: the stored name carries the site's own name and road as the booking system gives them ('Site, Loop: 030 Rte 144 Pines, Rte 144'); nothing to change.
Equestrian check: the Susquehannock camping page names the Dyer and Horsey Hilton equestrian areas; this entry is neither and its page(s) list no horse category.

Susquehannock advisories page (read 2026-11-10): district office closure Oct 17-18, 2026; Rausch Road reopened July 31, 2025; 'Stay Alert for ATVs on Roads' (the Northcentral Regional ATV Trail uses some PennDOT, township and forest roads); a dust advisory. No road closure, gate, bridge limit or timber-sale notice, and nothing on this entry's road. The camping page publishes no seasonal closure or site rotation.
